notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Jeremiah 2 this time. My research tool shut off before I could read a single page.

My first step requested three verse-by-verse sources at once:
- https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/jeremiah-2/
- https://www.preceptaustin.org/jeremiah-2-commentary
- https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jeremiah/2-13.htm

A coding error on my side meant the pages' text never reached me. When I tried to look again, the tool said I had no calls left for this turn. I have no search results or page text to work from.

You asked me to report only what the pages say and to give a URL for every point. So I haven't written any notes from memory, because they would be unsourced.

If you ask me to try again, I'll read pages one at a time:
1. **Traditional reading:** Enduring Word and Precept Austin, then the Bible Hub and StudyLight pages for Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary, covering verses 1–37.
2. **Protestant differences:** I'll search the tradition sites on the verses where views most likely split, such as v. 13 (the fountain and the broken cisterns), v. 22 (guilt that washing can't remove) and v. 35 ("I have not sinned"). These are themes of sin, grace and assurance.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey, Catholic and Orthodox sources such as New Advent (the Church Fathers on "living water" in v. 13), and any page on these sites that discusses prosperity, word of faith or hyper-grace teaching on this chapter.
